title: Shadow Traffic / Shadow Evals Kickoff Notes (Console & Tooling)
content:
Doc purpose
- Capture kickoff discussion + align across Console/Tooling, Policy Engine, Telemetry, Applied ML/Evals, SRE, Security.
- This is working notes (not a PRD). Expect open questions.

Meeting
- Date: 2025-09-24
- Duration: 60 min
- Facilitator: Talia Benson
- Notes: Dylan Brooks

Attendees
- Product
  - Marissa Cole (Console & Rollouts)
  - Paula Mendes (Rollout policy PM)
- Engineering (Console/Tooling)
  - Dylan Brooks (Eng lead)
  - Chloe Martin (Console backend)
  - Jada Williams (Rollouts/A-B backend)
  - Jin Woo Park (A/B testing + metrics)
- Platform / Policy / Routing
  - Ethan Park (Control-plane/policy lead)
  - Benji Okafor (Policy/config)
  - Mina Haddad (Smart routing)
- Telemetry & Analytics
  - Logan Wright (Telemetry platform)
  - Nadia Rahman (Cost/metering)
- Applied ML / Evals
  - Jonas Weber (Evals lead)
  - Selene Huang (Quality signals)
- SRE / Observability
  - Sean Gallagher (SRE lead)
- Security & Compliance
  - Naomi Feldman (Security/compliance product)
- Design
  - Kenji Nakamura (Rollouts UX)
  - Alicia Perez (Dashboards UX)

High-level summary (what we aligned on)
- We are building “Shadow Traffic” as an execution path that mirrors a sampled subset of live requests to one or more shadow targets and runs them asynchronously.
- Strict invariant: shadowing must never block or alter the primary response. Shadow failures are not user-visible.
- The feature is only valuable if we can (a) link shadow runs to the primary request, (b) compute stable comparative metrics, and (c) surface those metrics in Console and allow rollout policies to gate/hold/rollback.
- Guardrails are first-class: kill switch, capacity budgets, rate limits, and metric cardinality limits are required for beta.

Customer problem statement (from Marissa/Paula)
- Customers want to evaluate model upgrades and config changes with production-shaped traffic without impacting end-user responses.
- Offline evals are helpful but don’t capture real prompt distributions, tool-calling patterns, or customer-specific formatting constraints.
- Target use cases:
  1) Model upgrade: “Can we move route X from model A to model B without quality regression?”
  2) Config change: quantization profile / decoding changes / prompt template changes.
  3) Routing policy change: fallbacks, region routing.

Definitions / vocabulary
- Primary request: the user-facing request handled by the configured route.
- Shadow target: a candidate model/version/config (and later possibly prompt config) executed using the mirrored request.
- Shadow run: one execution of a mirrored request against a shadow target.
- Shadow eval metrics: quality + performance + cost metrics computed for a set of shadow runs, often aggregated by route and target.
- Join key: request_id that ties primary request metadata to shadow runs.

Non-goals (explicitly called out)
- Not a replacement for offline benchmark suites / eval harness.
- Not “ground truth correctness” for all tasks. We are looking for repeatable comparative signals (regression detection, gating).

Initial requirements (v0 / beta scope)
1) Policy / config (control plane)
- Per-route configuration to enable shadowing:
  - Sampling rate (%) with safe defaults.
  - Allowed customers / projects allowlist (at least: enterprise opt-in list).
  - Region scoping (optional in v0; at minimum must not violate residency requirements).
  - 1..N shadow targets (at least N=1 for MVP; preference is N up to 3 for beta).
- Global kill switch and per-route disable controls.

2) Data plane execution
- Shadow execution must be asynchronous, with strict isolation from the primary request path.
- Must enforce capacity budgets (queue + rate limiting). If shadow budget exceeded, drop shadow work (do not degrade primary).
- Timeouts: shadow run can have separate timeout budget; timeouts are recorded as shadow failures.

3) Linking primary <-> shadow
- We need deterministic linking between primary request and its shadow runs via request_id.
- Primary metadata captured for joins/filters:
  - route_id / route_name (or stable route key)
  - customer_id / project_id (with controls)
  - region
  - model_id (primary)
  - request characteristics (input token count, output token count, tool-calling vs not, streaming vs not)

4) Metrics (what we want to compute / store)
- Performance:
  - latency_ms (end-to-end, and where possible: queue wait vs inference time)
  - tokens/sec (approx)
  - error rate / timeout rate
- Cost:
  - token counts, estimated $ cost deltas
- Quality (beta)
  - Format adherence: JSON schema validity / structured output validity when configured
  - Similarity signals: embedding similarity / normalized edit distance for “expected similar” tasks (TBD)
  - Safety outcomes: policy pass/fail (at least: same safety classifier used for primary)
  - LLM-as-judge preference score (shadow vs primary) with clear disclaimers

5) Console
- A “Shadow Evals” view that answers:
  - For route X, shadow target Y: did quality improve/regress? what is win-rate? what is latency/cost delta?
  - Slice by region, time window, customer allowlist (only where permitted), model version.
- Minimum viable UI elements for beta:
  - Time-series of win-rate / error rate / latency delta
  - Breakdown table: route → target → key metrics
  - Filters: time range, route, target, region
  - Clear “non-impacting” explanation + quota indicators

6) Rollout gating integration
- Rollout policies should be able to reference a small set of stable metrics:
  - Example gates: “halt canary if judge win-rate drops > 3%” OR “halt if format_invalid_rate increases > 0.5%”.
- Need a decision on when gates evaluate (time window, minimum sample size).

Open questions (captured live)
A) Sampling semantics
- Is sampling applied before or after auth / quota checks?
  - Leaning: after auth, only mirror requests that would succeed primary checks.
- Do we sample by request or by conversation/session?
  - For chat, sampling by request is simpler but may bias multi-turn analysis. We can start with request-based sampling and revisit.
- Do we need deterministic sampling (hash of request_id) to keep comparability across deploys?
  - Strong preference from analytics: yes, deterministic sampling helps reduce “moving target” issues.

B) request_id propagation / compatibility
- Where does request_id originate for OpenAI-compatible endpoints?
  - Need to confirm whether gateway already generates a stable ID across retries.
- If primary retries internally, do we want the same request_id for the overall operation or per attempt?
  - For v0, treat each attempt as separate “request attempt id” but preserve a “root_request_id” for analysis (might be too much for beta).

C) What exactly do we store?
- Do we store full prompt + full output for each shadow run?
  - Security stance: default should be “do not store raw payloads”; store only derived metrics and redacted samples under restricted access.
- Do we store tool call arguments/results?
  - Likely “no” by default; if we store anything, it must be redacted and behind explicit allowlist + retention controls.

D) LLM-as-judge reliability
- Which tasks are safe to gate on?
  - Applied ML asked we avoid over-relying on judge for factuality. Safer: formatting adherence + safety + regression detection for style/structure.
- Calibration: do we need per-route judge prompts?
  - Plan: ship a minimal rubric template with optional per-route overrides later.

E) UI / UX and terminology
- What do we call it externally? “Shadow Evals” vs “Shadow Traffic” vs “Silent Canary”.
  - Tentative: “Shadow Evals” in Console, “Shadow Traffic” in API/config docs.
- How do we explain that it doesn’t affect the user response but can increase billed usage?
  - Product to define billing language and quota presentation (ties to PM-613).

F) Cardinality / tagging
- Which dimensions are allowed to tag metrics with?
  - Need strict allowlist; no freeform tags from customers.
- How do we represent target model/config in tags without exploding cardinality?
  - Proposed: use canonical “shadow_target_id” (short) + maintain a mapping table.

G) Capacity budgets / SLO
- What is the default sampling rate for beta?
  - SRE recommendation: 0% default, explicit opt-in; hard cap per route and global.
- What is the acceptable overhead envelope?
  - Non-negotiable: no measurable primary p99 regression. Shadow failures should never page as primary incidents.

Early design direction (rough consensus)
- Architecture direction: mirror + enqueue, then shadow runner executes asynchronously.
- Isolation: shadow runner uses separate worker pool / queue so primary runtime isn’t contended.
- Backpressure: dropping shadow work is acceptable; must emit “dropped_due_to_budget” metrics.
- Linking: request_id must be included in both primary and shadow telemetry events.

Beta success criteria (strawman)
- At least 2 design partners can run shadow evals on a real route for at least 7 days.
- Console can show:
  - judge win-rate trend
  - format invalid rate
  - latency and cost deltas
- SRE confirms no primary-path latency regression (within agreed budget) during enabled shadowing.
- Security confirms retention/redaction controls are implemented + auditable.

Task breakdown (initial)
1) Control plane + policy engine (Ethan/Benji)
- RoutePolicy schema additions: shadow enable + sampling + targets + allowlists
- Validation + safe defaults + migrations
- Global kill switch + per-route disable (coord with SRE)

2) Data plane / shadow runner (owner tbd; Console/Tooling coordinating)
- Async execution worker
- Queue + backpressure
- Timeouts and error handling
- Emit run-level telemetry events

3) Telemetry pipelines + datasets (Logan/Nadia)
- Event schema for shadow_run_started / completed / failed / dropped
- Aggregation jobs to compute rollup metrics per route/target/region/time
- Join strategy to primary request metadata

4) Applied ML / judge scoring (Jonas/Selene)
- Judge prompt template v1 + normalization
- Decide minimal set of judge-derived KPIs
- Guidance on interpreting judge results (known failure modes)

5) Console backend + UI (Chloe + Kenji/Alicia)
- Backend query APIs for rollups and comparisons
- UI MVP: dashboard + filters + breakdown tables
- Feature flags for beta

6) SRE / operational readiness (Sean)
- Capacity budget defaults and alerting strategy
- Load test plan for various sampling rates
- Incident runbook + kill switch verification steps

7) Security & compliance (Naomi)
- Data retention defaults (metrics vs payload)
- Redaction rules and access controls
- Audit logging requirements for any payload sample access

Decisions made in meeting (tentative)
- Default state is OFF (0% sampling) and requires explicit per-route enable.
- Dropping shadow work under backpressure is acceptable; must be observable.
- Console should present quality + performance deltas, not raw outputs by default.
- First release focuses on comparative metrics vs primary (shadow vs primary), not absolute scoring.

Action items
- Dylan: write up kickoff notes + circulate to stakeholders (this doc). Due 2025-09-26.
- Marissa/Paula: confirm beta partner list + what routes they’ll shadow; capture required quality metrics per partner. Due 2025-10-04.
- Ethan/Benji: draft RoutePolicy schema fields and validation rules; bring to next sync. Due 2025-10-01.
- Logan/Nadia: propose telemetry event schema + minimal dimensions + aggregation plan. Due 2025-10-02.
- Jonas/Selene: propose judge rubric v1 and where it is safe to gate. Due 2025-10-07.
- Sean: propose initial capacity budget defaults + required alerts + kill-switch semantics. Due 2025-10-07.
- Naomi: outline retention/redaction defaults + opt-out/controls needed for beta. Due 2025-10-08.
- Kenji/Alicia: first-pass Console IA (information architecture) for “Shadow Evals” dashboard + naming. Due 2025-10-09.

Next meetings / cadence
- Weekly shadow-evals sync (30 min) starting week of 2025-09-30.
- Separate technical deep dive for request_id propagation + deterministic sampling (Dylan/Ethan/Logan) TBD.

Notes / parking lot
- “Prompt config shadowing” (changing system prompt/templates) is highly desired but touches sensitive payload storage + versioning; likely GA follow-up unless we can do it without storing raw content.
- Need to align with pricing/packaging early: shadow runs create real compute cost; must show quotas and attribution in billing analytics.
- Tool-calling: define whether shadow target is allowed to call tools. For beta, recommend forcing tool calls OFF in shadow unless deterministic sandbox exists (to avoid side effects). If OFF, we need a metric tag noting tool calls were suppressed.
